concepts.def: EM wave; no mass or charge

walkthroughs.body_html:
Alpha: mass -4, atomic -2.

Beta-minus: mass unchanged, atomic +1.

Gamma: no change to mass or atomic number.

After 1 half-life: half the activity.

After 2 half-lives: a quarter. After 3: an eighth.

Activity halves every half-life.

Predict by counting how many half-lives have passed.

mcqs.q: Alpha emission changes a nucleus by:
Half-life of 8 hours; after 24 hours, fraction left:
What did Rutherford's alpha-scattering experiment show about the atom?
options: It showed that atoms are solid spheres of positive charge with electrons embedded inside.
The nucleus shrinks to half its original size after one half-life.
Most of the atom is empty space, with a tiny dense positive nucleus.
It showed that alpha particles can pass through any material because they are massless.

mcqs.q: Which type of nuclear radiation is most ionising?
options: Gamma is most ionising because it can travel furthest and pass through almost anything.
Beta radiation is most ionising because it consists of fast electrons.
Alpha radiation — large, doubly charged particles cause the most ionisation per unit distance.
The nucleus shrinks to half its original size after one half-life.

mcqs.q: After one half-life, what happens to an individual radioactive nucleus?
options: The nucleus shrinks to half its original size after one half-life.
Beta radiation is most ionising because it consists of fast electrons.
It has a 50 percent chance of having decayed — radioactive decay is random for any single nucleus.
Every nucleus is guaranteed to have half-decayed after one half-life.
